about: D-SRC-73 (2026-10-27): what the helper answers when a folder it writes into cannot be used, and the sentence the shell shows for it. The helper's code and the model's sentence are joined by a NAME, so both sides run this file (rule 13): tests/test_local_refusals.py applies each `damage` in a scratch directory, runs the REAL helper as a subprocess with `argv` (HOME, the XDG folders and PATH in the scratch directory, so nothing of the user's is read and no mpv can start), and compares its stdout with `reply` exactly, with `{dir}` the damaged folder, `{fixtures}` tests/fixtures, `{cache}` a seeded cache folder and `{id}` its first channel; tests/Model.test.js maps `reply` through Model.parseHelperStatus and Model.statusReason and compares `reason`, with `{dir}` a path under a home directory, and checks that the reason names no path and that Model.failureFromHost puts no host after it. Damages: `folder-link` -- {dir} is a symbolic link to a name that does not exist; `folder-file` -- a regular file is at {dir}; `parent-0500` -- {dir} does not exist and its parent is mode 0500 (skipped when the tests run as root, who is not refused); `lock-dir` -- {dir} is a 0700 folder with a folder at the player's lock file name, `player.lock`. D-PLY-30 (2026-10-27) added the player cases: `player start|restart|stop` answer in their own reply shape, `folder_unusable` (R25c's sentence) for a runtime folder that is a link to nothing, and `runtime_unwritable` (which of the two, the error's words, no path) for a runtime folder that cannot be made or a lock file that cannot be opened. D-PLY-31 (2026-10-28) added `socket-file` -- {dir} is a 0700 folder with a regular file at the player's socket name, `mpv.sock`; `mpv-not-executable` -- PATH holds an `mpv` that is mode 0644; `fork-refused` -- the helper runs under RLIMIT_NPROC 0, set in its own process before the exec (skipped as root, who is not refused); `pipes-refused` -- the helper runs with every descriptor from 3 up to two below RLIMIT_NOFILE taken, so it holds the player's lock in one of the last two and the spawn cannot have the two a pipe needs. D-SRC-74 (2026-10-28) added the cache key verbs, with `{root}` the cache folder and `{key}` a source key: `key-file` -- a regular file is at {dir}, `{root}/sources/{key}`; `sources-link` -- {dir}, `{root}/sources`, is a symbolic link to a name that does not exist. `otherRefusals` (2026-10-28, D-PLY-31, D-PLY-34, D-EPG-13) holds replies that do not fit the checks over `refusals`, which take every case to be this machine's and told at once: the guide's own refusals are the PROVIDER'S (`host: kept` -- a line that composes `from <host>` keeps it, D-SRC-71's reading), the player lock's `busy` is retried before it is told (`retried`), `too_large` is the helper's own memory only on a player verb, and the clipboard's `spawn_failed` reaches no surface at all (`surface: none`; Model.parseClipboardReply drops every failure). Damages: `fresh` -- {dir} is a new 0700 cache folder, and the verb may write nothing but its status file there; `lock-held` -- the test holds the player lock in {dir}; `out-of-memory` -- the verb runs in the test's own process through the helper's main() with MemoryError raised where it reads the channel list (`read_channel_document`, which `load_channels` and player_target both read through since 2026-10-29), the exact reply main() gives any MemoryError; `wl-paste-not-executable` -- PATH holds a `wl-paste` that is mode 0644. `{int}` stands for the run's own durationMs, any whole number of milliseconds.
